To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the substitution effects of bay functionalization and thio group on the absorption of PDIs were disclosed, and the mechanism of the substitution was also revealed by DFT calculation.
thionation of PDI derivatives can effectively narrow their band gap, while electron donating group decorated PDI derivatives are promising for red shift of their absorption.
the bay functionalization and thionication of PDI are both effective to tune its absorption into NIR region, which is desirable for potential application.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and synthesis of PDI derivatives, which can be used as NIR-absorbing materials for potential application in the future.
the design of NIR-absorbing materials based on PDI derivatives and the substitution effect on their absorption is disclosed by DFT calculation.
the design and calculation of the optical property of PDI derivatives.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
thionation is a more effective method to tune the optical properties of PDI than bay functionalization.
the bay area functionalization is a more effective strategy for NIR absorption than thionation, which could be a promising candidate for further application.
the bay functionalization and thiolation of the PDI are both feasible and effective approaches to tune its optical properties, and thionation is more favorable for NIR absorption.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
thionation and bay area electron donating group are the most effective strategy for NIR absorption of PDI, and the imine group in bay area is essential for the formation of conjugated structure.
bay area functionalization is more effective than thionation in terms of BG narrowing and spectral red shift.
the bay position is the best site for functionalization and thio substitution is the most effective way to tune the optical properties of PDI derivatives.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the bay area of PDI is a good place to introduce substituent to tune the absorption spectrum and the imine group should be retained in the PDI derivatives to ensure the conjugation between substituent and the framework.

the substitution of PDI with electron donating group at the bay position and thionation at the carbonyl position are the most effective ways to narrow band gap and shift absorption to the NIR region, which is of great importance for the application of PDI in photovoltaics and optoelectronic devices.
the thionated PDI is the best candidate for the NIR absorption.
